title: Engram-internal origin/store identity and minimal host joining configuration for decentralized task sync
outcome: Engram-internal origin/store identity and minimal host joining configuration for decentralized task sync
acceptance: Each store enrolled for task sync has a stable Engram-owned origin identity, minted by the explicit enrollment as an additive canonical record, distinct from its display alias and from process boot. It survives restart and is usable by CLI-only Engram. A store that never enrolls needs no conversion, and ordinary store opening stays strict and never writes the identity implicitly.

A detected clone/restore or broken continuity quarantines pending exchange operations for explicit reconciliation, and a new install never silently adopts another origin's write authority, with tests for restart, clone and restore (including restoring an older copy that carries the same origin)

A new host joins with explicit local configuration (its own identity, project binding, configured remote and branch, opt-in). An empty target may bootstrap, and a store with existing independent tasks joins through the resolved merged-graph path under w-65fb79ead0c3; neither loses local planning or transfers claims, grants, runtime or evidence authority.
Any durable-format change is named, judged under the full-store migration rule and presented to Greg before landing; today's asserted --origin-machine alias is not silently reinterpreted
